generations.label: A
generations.title: Conservative
text: The Coherence Thesis is an invitation to recognize that the future of civilization will not be decided by technology or ideology, but by whether we learn to organize society around the biological conditions that make intelligence, trust, and coordination possible at planetary scale.

Our crises present as political, ideological, and technological. Beneath them lies a biological oversight. Any viable post-extractive future must be built on coherence as the substrate that sustains collective intelligence, in a world whose interdependence, velocity, and entanglement have outrun every inherited form of coordination.

This book is written for the moment when our technological power has begun to exceed the coherence with which we wield it, and when recognizing that mismatch may decide whether civilization adapts, hardens, or collapses.

reasoning.note: Paragraph 1 unchanged from the baseline. Its spine, not by A or B but by C, carries a long sentence without strain.

Introduced a diagnostic verb that earns the biological claim following it.

rulings.question: Which of the first three variants is closest?
rulings.decision: A, by a clear margin. B and C are not approved.
rulings.rationale: A preserves the invitational opening intact. B and C buy concision from register and from the argument's only causal account.

rulings.question: Must the breath marks be preserved?
rulings.decision: No. The glyphs may go. Their positions remain informative for flow and pacing.
rulings.rationale: Author decision. The pacing they encoded must survive as paragraph structure.

rulings.question: Is the comma that replaced an em dash acceptable?
rulings.decision: No. It reads as more verbose than necessary.
rulings.rationale: Author identified the fused sentence as slack. Produced R-PUNCT-STRUCT.

rulings.question: Is paragraph 2 of A1 acceptable?
rulings.decision: No. It still ends with a run-on.
rulings.rationale: Author identified the trailing clause. Produced R-LAND.

rulings.question: Does the close read correctly?
rulings.decision: No. It speaks of the mismatch as though already past. Use the proximal form.
rulings.rationale: Author asked for exploration of tense and deixis. Produced R-DEIXIS.

rulings.question: How are derived variants named?
rulings.decision: Positional descent. A child of A is A1, its child A11. A sibling branch from A is A2.
rulings.rationale: Label and grid position then carry the same information, so ancestry renders without a separate field.

rulings.question: Does tightening a hedged verb phrase in paragraph 1 cost too much?
rulings.rationale: Editorial craft decision taken under delegated authority. The hedge carried a useful admission, but the invitational stance is carried by the opening noun and by the address to the reader, both of which survive. The hierarchy of fidelity ranks the preserved stance above the lost hedge, and R-PROPORTION is satisfied at 15 percent.
rulings.note: Superseded by the voice card clause on load-bearing admissions of uncertainty.

rulings.question: Do voice cards require author approval?
rulings.decision: No. The editorial agent holds responsibility for editorial guidelines, including voice cards.
rulings.rationale: Author delegation, 2026-07-29. Canon, doctrine, and claim content remain author decisions.

regenerationTest.purpose: The approved text is stored as evidence, not as a template. The rules must be sufficient to reproduce it from the baseline without consulting it.
regenerationTest.method: Applied only editorial/method/standard.md and the revised volume-01 voice card to the baseline section, then compared against A11.

divergences.observation: The rules keep 'learn to organize society' where A11 cut it.

divergences.verdict: The rules are right and RU7 is wrong. A hedge that concedes the method is not yet known belongs to an invitational stance. RU7 is superseded by the card clause. The section should retain the phrase.
divergences.action: RU7 marked superseded. A11 is evidence of the path taken, not the text to ship.

divergences.observation: The rules split paragraph 2 into four sentences by promoting the trailing clause, but keep the baseline's 'at planetary scale' and 'total systemic entanglement' where A11 had compressed them.
divergences.cause: R-PROPORTION forbids cutting what is not defective. Those phrases carry scope and are not surplus.
divergences.verdict: The rules are right. A11 compressed by preference rather than by defect.

divergences.observation: Regeneration lands at 2 percent below baseline, far under the 10 to 18 percent this voice card sets as the volume's expected compression.
divergences.cause: The expectation was derived from the volume as a whole. The orientation is dense, deliberate prose with few defects, so correct editing barely compresses it.
divergences.verdict: The expectation is a volume level guide, not a section level target. Recorded so no future pass treats the range as a quota to reach.
divergences.action: Volume-01 voice card states the range as a volume expectation. Do not apply it per section.

divergences.observation: Regeneration restored the baseline phrase the scale of, which variant A had cut and the author had approved cutting.

regenerationTest.conclusion: Converged on round two. Round one derived from the baseline with nine rules and left three transformations unexplained: a negation stack restated as appearance and reality, a perfect form reduced to simple present, and a generic verb replaced by one from the volume signature register. Each became a named obligation, and round two reproduced the approved text exactly, 112 words against 112. The rules were applied by the same agent that knew the target, so this is evidence of sufficiency rather than proof of independence.

rulesInForce.obligation: The voice card is binding. An edit that contradicts it is a defect.
Change proportional to the defect. Explain reductions past a third.
The catalog is not complete. Its silence is not proof a construction is sound.
A prohibited mark is a structural signal. Rebuild the syntax to do its work.
Every catalog entry has a defect limb and a retention limb. Record which applies.
Remove must name what was contributed and where it went.
Preserve alternation of sentence lengths. Length alone is not a defect.
Paragraphs end on a concrete beat, not a trailing clause.
Hold the reader in the present where the text names a live condition.
Do not stack denials before the claim. Restate as appearance then reality.
Prefer the simple present for a live condition unless the timing is load bearing.
Prefer the volume signature register over a generic near synonym of equal precision.
